title: MYP Individuals and Societies and University…
summary: Learn how MYP Individuals and Societies affects university applications, later IB choices, transcripts, skills, and your subject selection decision.
body_markdown:
**MYP Individuals and Societies usually has a limited direct effect on university applications.** Universities generally focus on your final upper-secondary qualification, such as the IB Diploma, A levels, or a national school-leaving credential. However, the subject can matter indirectly through your transcript, preparation for later humanities courses, MYP Certificate eligibility, and access to Diploma Programme subjects.


Choose Individuals and Societies based on your school's requirements, future subject options, interests, and workload. Do not take it simply because you assume every university expects it.


### How much do universities care about MYP Individuals and Societies?


For most undergraduate applicants, an MYP Individuals and Societies grade is **not a primary admissions requirement** . Universities commonly publish requirements involving final qualifications, overall scores, and specific advanced subjects. Applicants to mathematics, science, economics, or language-related degrees may need particular Higher Level subjects or equivalent courses.


MYP results can still form part of your academic record. Their importance depends on the application system:


Application situation Likely importance


University mainly assesses IB Diploma results Low compared with predicted and final DP grades


University requests several years of transcripts May provide supporting evidence of progress


Country requires an age-16 qualification Official MYP results may have an equivalency role


School uses MYP performance for DP placement Could affect access to a preferred Group 3 subject


**Recognition is not the same as direct admission.** The IB's[university recognition guidance](https://ibo.org/university-admission/find-countries-and-universities-that-recognize-the-ib/) provides general information, but applicants must confirm current requirements with each university.


### What the MYP officially requires


Individuals and Societies is one of the MYP's eight subject groups. According to the official[MYP curriculum overview](https://ibo.org/programmes/middle-years-programme/curriculum/) , schools normally provide at least **50 teaching hours** in each subject group during each programme year. Subject-group flexibility is possible in Years 4 and 5 under specified conditions, but choices remain subject to IB rules, local requirements, and school policy.


The group can include history, geography, economics, politics, philosophy, business management, sociology, psychology, and related disciplines. Schools may organize these as discrete subjects, modules, or an integrated humanities course, as described in the IB's[Individuals and Societies overview](https://ibo.org/programmes/middle-years-programme/curriculum/individuals-and-societies/) .


For students pursuing the **IB MYP Certificate** , the subject has greater formal importance. The[MYP passing criteria](https://ibo.org/about-the-ib/what-it-means-to-be-an-ib-student/recognizing-student-achievement/about-assessment/myp-passing-criteria/) include an Individuals and Societies on-screen assessment among the certificate components. Ask your coordinator whether you are registered for the full certificate, individual course results, or only school-based grades.


### How the subject can matter indirectly


### Preparation for later IB subjects


MYP Individuals and Societies develops source evaluation, research, argumentation, data interpretation, and critical thinking. These skills transfer to DP History, Geography, Economics, Global Politics, Business Management, Psychology, and Digital Society.


You do not necessarily need a matching MYP discipline before beginning every DP Group 3 subject. School progression policies are more important. One school might permit DP Economics without prior economics but expect strong mathematics, while another may use MYP humanities results when recommending students for History HL.


Before making an **MYP Individuals and Societies subject choice** , ask:


- Which DP subjects does this course prepare me for?
- Does my school require a particular course or grade for DP entry?
- Could changing the course affect MYP Certificate eligibility?
- Does assessment emphasize essays, data, fieldwork, or source analysis?
- Which option best matches my strengths and possible plans?


Course structures differ between schools. RevisionDojo's guide to[how schools customize MYP subject choices](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/choice-of-subjects-how-schools-customize-myp-for-local-needs) explains why course titles alone may not reveal what students actually study.


### Transcripts and transferable skills


Universities requesting a complete secondary transcript may see MYP grades and academic progression. One weak result is unlikely to decide an application, while consistent achievement or later improvement can support the broader picture of academic readiness. The[RevisionDojo overview of MYP university recognition](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/myp-university-recognition) distinguishes school grades, official course results, and the MYP Certificate.


Individuals and Societies also teaches students to evaluate sources, compare perspectives, explain causes and consequences, interpret statistics, and construct defensible conclusions. These abilities support humanities, law, business, social sciences, environmental studies, and evidence-based writing. The value comes from demonstrated skills rather than the course title alone.


### When should you prioritize the subject?


Prioritize Individuals and Societies if you enjoy analysing institutions, places, human behaviour, historical change, or economic decisions. It is particularly useful if you may pursue a humanities or social science subject in the DP and want more practice with research and extended writing.


Do not assume that a specialized title automatically impresses universities. An integrated humanities course can address the same MYP objectives as a discrete history or geography course. However, avoid choosing an additional humanities option if it would displace mathematics, science, or another subject needed for a likely future pathway.


### A practical subject-selection method


Use this order when comparing options:


1. **Confirm school rules.** Identify compulsory subjects and any MYP Certificate requirements.
2. **Consider broad directions.** Explore several possible degree areas without committing prematurely.
3. **Check later prerequisites.** Review representative university pages for required senior-secondary subjects.
4. **Work backwards.** Determine which MYP choices preserve access to those later courses.
5. **Compare assessment styles.** Consider whether you perform best in essays, investigations, data analysis, or source work.
6. **Protect balance.** Avoid an unnecessarily demanding or writing-heavy programme chosen only for appearance.


The IB publishes official[DP course-selection guidance](https://ibo.org/university-admission/support-students-transition-to-higher-education/course-selection-guidance/) . RevisionDojo's[guide to choosing IB subjects](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-subject-guides-choose-ib-subjects) can also help students compare content, levels, assessment, and university prerequisites.


### Common mistakes to avoid


Do not assume universities universally require MYP History, Geography, or Economics for related degrees. Published criteria usually emphasize later qualifications. Also distinguish ordinary school grades from IB-validated course results and the full MYP Certificate, especially where age-16 equivalency matters.


Finally, compare actual units and assessments rather than choosing by name. RevisionDojo's overview of[the eight MYP subject groups](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/what-subjects-are-taught-in-myp) provides context for evaluating the programme as a whole.


### Conclusion


MYP Individuals and Societies matters mainly as **preparation and academic context** , not as a universal university entrance requirement. Its importance increases when it affects certificate eligibility, appears on a full transcript, or determines access to a later DP subject.


Choose the course that supports realistic options and suits your abilities. RevisionDojo's Study Notes, Flashcards, and Questionbank can then help strengthen the analytical skills the subject assesses.
